purpose: Teach: 感傷/従順/習性/一服/四角い/極まりない/輝か/育む

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは感傷を表に出されない方だった
lines.en: Gran, when he was younger, your father never showed his feelings on the surface.
lines.style: Soft, remembering voice. Eyes distant and focused on something far away. Gentle cadence, as if sorting through decades of small moments. Pause before 'never' — the weight of that choice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、孫に従順を求められなかったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: No, that's right — grandfather never demanded obedience from his grandchildren, did he?
lines.style: Affirming, warm. Her voice carries the certainty of someone who lived it. Gentle tilt upward at 'did he?' — not a question, but an invitation to remember together. Slightly breathy, intimate.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが朝早起きする習性をお持ちだった
lines.en: Gran, when he was younger, your father would always wake up before dawn.
lines.style: Reverent, almost hushed. The detail surfaces like a cherished photograph. Slow delivery. His voice steadies around 'dawn' — the consistency of it matters to him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年は縁側で一服されてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: In his later years, he'd sit on the veranda having a cigarette, wouldn't he?
lines.style: Gentle, pictorial. She's drawing the scene in air. Warm affection underneath. The pause after 'veranda' — she can see him there. Soft closing, intimate address.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが四角い升で米を量られた
lines.en: Gran, when he was younger, your father would measure the rice with those square wooden boxes.
lines.style: Precise, almost meditative. The specificity of the object anchors him. Quiet reverence. His breath catches slightly on 'wooden boxes' — a small, exact thing that meant something.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご家族への愛情は極まりないものでしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandfather, his love for the family was boundless, wasn't it?
lines.style: Confident, tender assertion. Not asking for confirmation — stating what she knows to be true. Her voice settles on 'boundless' with certainty. The final address carries deep affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんの瞳がいつも輝かれてた
lines.en: Gran, when he was younger, your father's eyes were always bright.
lines.style: Voice catches with emotion held in check. The image is vivid for him. Slow, careful articulation of 'always' — that constancy matters. Trailing breath, as if he can still see it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様を育む祖父でいらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were such a nurturing grandfather to your grandchildren, weren't you?
lines.style: Soft, affirming closure. Her voice wraps around the words gently. Reaching toward him with warmth. The final address breathes with deep affection and recognition. Almost tender silence after.
